subject: Re: Post-demo: data governance checklist & marketplace vendor mapping
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finedge.com>

Cc: dpo@finedge.com

Subject: Follow-up from today's demo — data handling clarifications

Thanks for the demo today — it was helpful. A couple of quick follow-ups so we can make progress with procurement and our security review: 

1) PII scope: can you confirm whether any customer-provided PII is sent to 3rd-party telemetry vendors (for logs/metrics) or if that data is redacted before egress? We need explicit examples (e.g., user_id, email) and whether those fields are hashed or removed.

2) Retention: what are the default retention windows for request logs, transcript KV caches, and analytics telemetry? Are retention settings configurable per-tenant?

3) Marketplace vendors: you mentioned marketplace integrations can forward inference payloads to a partner. Which vendors in the marketplace receive request payloads today and under what contract terms (subprocessor list)?

If you can send a short checklist or a mapping doc we can attach to our risk assessment, that would be ideal.

Appreciate it — Emily

--
Emily Zhao
Head of Security Operations
FinEdge

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finedge.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-15T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — data handling clarifications

Hi Emily — great to meet you on the call. Thanks for the clear list. Summary answers below and a proposed next steps list at the bottom. I’ll attach a short mapping workbook (redwood-data-map.xlsx) with fields toggled for PII vs non-PII and current retention defaults.

PII scope and telemetry
- Redwood runtime does not intentionally send raw PII to telemetry vendors. Metrics (latency, error rates, token counts) are numeric-only.
- Request/response logs retained in our control plane are redacted by default: we hash any top-level fields labeled email or user_id using a salted HMAC before they reach third-party observability pipelines.
- Exceptions: customers who enable "verbose-proxy" (rare, opt-in) may forward payloads to a configured S3 endpoint or third-party analytics vendor; this must be enabled explicitly and appears in the tenant config and billing agreement.

Retention windows (defaults)
- Request logs (control plane): 90 days (configurable down to 7 days, up to 24 months with an enterprise add-on)
- KV cache traces (runtime debug): 7 days and only enabled for debug sessions; requires signed approval
- Marketplace telemetry (partner metrics): 180 days for aggregated metrics, no request-level transcripts unless customer enables forwarding

Marketplace/subprocessor flows
- Current marketplace vendors that receive forwarded payloads (opt-in by customer): MetricsCo (analytics@metricsco.com), TraceStack (ingest@tracestack.io). Both are under DPAs that prohibit retention of raw transcripts; we list them in our subprocessor registry.
- Cloud providers (AWS eu-west and us-east): object storage and ephemeral inference hosts; logs sent to cloud logging are hashed/redacted per the rules above.

Proposed next steps
1) I’ll share the redwood-data-map.xlsx and a one-page SOC2 excerpt in a follow-up email (attached).
2) If helpful, we can schedule a short technical call with Vivek to walk through tenant config controls and the marketplace vendor contract language.
3) If FinEdge wants a copy of our subprocessor registry and DPA excerpts, we can route that through your procurement contact.

Let me know which of the above you want first; I can also provide a tailored checklist for your security questionnaire.

Thanks,
Monica
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — data handling clarifications

Looping in technical details for the record — Emily asked about hashing and any edge cases where PII could be forwarded. Quick notes: 
- We perform field-based redaction at ingestion in the control plane. Hashing uses tenant-specific salt derived from the tenant id + a rotating system key; that prevents cross-tenant correlation.
- Marketplace integrations that perform "direct-forward" do so via explicit tenant configuration and require a signed integration consent. By default the marketplace provides metric-level integration only (no transcripts).
- For customers that need strict data residency, we can pin their private deployment to a VPC region and disable any marketplace-directed forwarding; that is captured in a Dedicated/Private deployment appendix.

Attachments to prepare (I'll drop into the shared Drive):
- redwood-data-map.xlsx (field-level mapping)
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC2 scope excerpt)
- marketplace-egress-diagram.png (architecture of marketplace forwarding)

If procurement wants exact contract language for the MetricsCo and TraceStack DPAs, procurement can request the DPA attachments; we'll manage redaction of any internal notes.

-Vivek
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
